note: Wren Phonics — Same-day boost guide (b410, 2026-10-08). Built from the research file §1D (keep-up as an idea, common SSP practice) in Wren's own words; the 3-week reassessment interval and ~30% re-teach threshold are cited as common practice, not hand-picked numbers. provenance: Wren original, b410, 2026-10-08.
who: Any child who, by the end of a lesson, is not yet secure with that lesson's own new content — not a fixed list of named children; who needs it changes lesson to lesson. Spot them from the "Have a go" and "Use it" parts of the main lesson, not a separate test.
when: The SAME day as the lesson it follows, before the end of that school day — never left until tomorrow, because tomorrow's lesson is taught assuming today's is already secure.
how_long: Short: 5 to 10 minutes is usually enough. This is a quick top-up in smaller steps, not a second full lesson.
group_size: 1:1 or a small group of children who all need the same thing today. A quiet, low-distraction spot, used consistently so children know what it means when they are called to it.
who_delivers: An adult who already knows the routine securely — ideally whoever taught the main lesson, or another adult briefed on exactly what that lesson covered, so the boost matches it exactly rather than drifting into something slightly different.
same_routine_smaller_steps: A boost session teaches the SAME content, the SAME way, just slower and with more repetition and a narrower focus — never a different activity, a different mnemonic, or a shortcut version. Re-run the same four-part shape (Warm up, New sound, Have a go, Use it) in miniature: say the sound together several times, rebuild the action and formation together, then blend/segment the exact words from today's lesson again before trying the mini-check below.
reassess: Reassess every 3 weeks, not just once: keep a simple running note of which boosts each child has needed, and check at the 3-week mark whether those same gaps have closed or whether a pattern is forming that needs a different response (e.g. a conversation with the room/class lead, or a look at whether the content itself needs re-teaching to the whole group — see below).
reteach_threshold: If roughly a THIRD (about 30% or more) of the group needed the same boost on the same piece of content, that is a signal about the whole-group teaching, not about those individual children — re-teach that content properly to the whole group before moving on, rather than running the same 1:1 boost for a third of the class one at a time.
never_a_different_programme: A child who needs a boost still learns to read through this same systematic synthetic phonics sequence — same GPCs, same order, same routine. Same-day boost adapts the PACE and GROUP SIZE of this one programme; it is never a switch to a different programme or a different method for a struggling child.
record_keeping: A short, honest note of what was boosted and how the child responded is more useful than a tick box — it is what tells you, three weeks later, whether the 3-week reassessment is actually finding something new or just confirming what you already knew.
